rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: let us think from Black's side, with Black to move. Game jan2500 × idrpughsmurf, Lichess 2020. The white rook has just captured on e5.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.e2: Recapturing with the rook on e8 looks natural. But that rook defends your rook on d8, which is attacked by the rook on d1.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.e3: An in-between move is a strong move, such as a check, played before the recapture everyone expects. The opponent has to answer it, and the recapture is still there.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.p: Find the in-between move, before recapturing on e5.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.certo: The rook captures the rook on d1 with check. White has to answer, and the rook on e5 is still attacked.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is the rook capturing on d1, with check. After it, the rook on e8 recaptures on e5.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.err.e8e5.1: The rook recaptures on e5, but it leaves e8, and your rook on d8 is left undefended.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.err.e8e5.2: With this move the rook on d1 captures your rook on d8 with check. White wins the rook back, and the game is level.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.err.e8e5.3: Back to the position: before recapturing on e5, see whether there is a move with check.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.fora: That move leaves the rook on e5 alive, and White keeps extra material. Look for a check before recapturing.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: the recapture on e5 can wait one move.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.l0: White has to get out of check before thinking about the rook on e5.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.l1: The knight on c3 recaptures on d1.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.l2: Now the rook on e8 recaptures on e5. Black is a rook up.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex1.l3: The check came before the recapture, and White had no time to save the rook on e5. In positions like this, before recapturing, look for a check or a capture the opponent has to answer.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: now with White, in the Game VEJICA × pro100Rival, Lichess 2020. The black bishop has just captured your knight on c3 and attacks your queen.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.e2: Recapturing with the queen looks natural. First, look at the knight on d7: it is pinned by your bishop on b5, because the king stands behind it, on e8.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.p: Find the in-between move, before recapturing on c3.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.certo: The bishop captures the knight on d7 with check. Black has to answer, and the bishop on c3 is still there to be recaptured.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is the bishop capturing the knight on d7, with check. Afterwards, the queen recaptures on c3.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.err.d2c3.1: The queen recaptures the bishop, and the pieces are simply traded.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.err.d2c3.2: With this move Black castles. The knight on d7 is no longer pinned, and the game is level.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.err.d2c3.3: Back to the position: before recapturing on c3, see what the bishop on b5 can capture.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.err.b2c3.1: The pawn recaptures the bishop, but it opens up your king's cover.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.err.b2c3.2: With this move the knight on e7 goes to d5 and attacks the pawn on c3. Your king is exposed, and Black is better.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.err.b2c3.3: Back to the position: before recapturing on c3, see what the bishop on b5 can capture.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not win the piece back, and Black keeps the knight it captured. Look for a check before recapturing.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: the recapture on c3 can wait one move.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.l0: Black has to get out of check before thinking about the bishop on c3.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.l1: The king goes to f8. If the queen on d8 recaptured on d7, your queen would capture it with check, supported by the rook on d1.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.l2: Now the queen recaptures the bishop on c3. White is a piece up.
rot.intermezzo.ideia.ex2.l3: Here the in-between move was a capture with check. In positions like this, look at the captures with check before the recapture: they give the opponent no time.
rot.intermezzo.demos.torre.1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side, in the Game PlemSovhoz × Pskov_rulit, Lichess 2021. The white rook has just captured your rook on c8.
rot.intermezzo.demos.torre.2: Recapturing with the rook on f8 looks natural. First, the queen captures the rook on b1, with check.
rot.intermezzo.demos.torre.3: The knight goes back to f1 to block the check.
rot.intermezzo.demos.torre.4: Only now does the rook recapture on c8. Black is a rook up and has the advantage.
rot.intermezzo.demos.torre.5: If the rook had recaptured at once, the rook on b1 would come to b8 and attack your rook on c8, and Black would lose material. In positions like this, capture with check the piece that is still attacking, before the recapture.
rot.intermezzo.demos.defensor.1: Attack: Black again, in the Game Isa-Xelilli × Derekchlong, Lichess 2021. The white knight has just captured on d4.
rot.intermezzo.demos.defensor.2: Recapturing with the bishop on g7 looks natural, but the bishop on f2 defends the knight, and your bishop would be captured.
rot.intermezzo.demos.defensor.3: First, the rook on c2 captures the defender: the bishop on f2.
rot.intermezzo.demos.defensor.4: The rook on f1 recaptures on f2.
rot.intermezzo.demos.defensor.5: Now the bishop captures the knight on d4, which was left undefended. And the rook on f2 is pinned: behind it, on the same diagonal, stands the king on g1.
rot.intermezzo.demos.defensor.6: The in-between move can also be a capture: here it removed the defender. In positions like this, see who defends the piece you want to recapture, and capture the defender first.
rot.intermezzo.demos.excecao.1: Attack: now with White, in the Game FirebirdXXX × Sagar_Udasi, Lichess 2022. The black rook has just captured on f3. The knight can give check on f6 before the recapture. Is a check enough here?
rot.intermezzo.demos.excecao.2: The knight gives check on f6.
rot.intermezzo.demos.excecao.3: The pawn on e7 captures the knight. The check threatened nothing: White simply gave up the knight, and the game is level.
rot.intermezzo.demos.excecao.4: A check that only gives the piece away, winning nothing, is not an in-between move. Back to the position: here, the best is to recapture at once.
rot.intermezzo.demos.excecao.5: The pawn on g2 recaptures the rook.
rot.intermezzo.demos.excecao.6: The queen captures the pawn with check.
rot.intermezzo.demos.excecao.7: Your queen goes to g2, blocks the check and offers the trade. White keeps extra material.
rot.intermezzo.demos.excecao.8: In positions like this, check what the in-between move forces. If the opponent answers and still keeps your piece, there is no in-between move: recapture.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.recaptura.enuncia: Now with White. The black rook has just captured on f5. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.recaptura.fim: Here the check with the queen won nothing, and the right move was to recapture at once. Then, when the black queen captured your queen, the rook gave check on f8 before recapturing: you are left with rook and pawn against three pawns.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.recaptura.err.d4f: The queen captures the queen with check, but the rook on f5 recaptures on f6. The queens are simply traded, you miss the chance to recapture the rook, and Black is better. Before a check, see what it wins.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.recaptura.err2.c4: The rook recaptures the queen, but the rook on f8 recaptures your rook on f5, and Black is better. Before recapturing the queen, look for a check.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.cavalo.enunciado: Now with Black. The white rook has just captured on e8 and attacks your rook on f8. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.cavalo.fim: Recapturing at once left the game level. The queen captured the knight on f3 with check, defended by the knight on e5, and only then did the rook recapture on e8: you won a piece.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.cavalo.err.f8e8: The rook recaptures, and the game is level: the knight on f3 is still alive. Before recapturing, see whether there is a stronger move.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.cavalo.err.e5f3: The knight captures the knight, but the rook on e8 captures your rook on f8 with check, and the game is level. Look for a capture with check.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.cavalo.err2.e5g4: That move leaves the white rook on e8 alive, and White keeps extra material. Recapture the rook now.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.cavalo.err2.e5d3: That move leaves the white rook on e8 alive, and White keeps extra material. Recapture the rook now.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.bispo.enunciado: White again. The black queen has just captured your queen on a3. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.bispo.fim: Recapturing at once left the game level. The knight captured the bishop on f6 with check, and the rook recaptured the queen afterwards: you won a bishop.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.bispo.err.a1a3: The rook recaptures the queen, and the game is level. Before recapturing, see whether there is a stronger move.
rot.intermezzo.pratica.bispo.err2.f6e8: The knight captures the rook on e8, but the black queen escapes from a3, and you are left without your queen. Recapture the queen now.
